Hi Marta —

Thanks for the clear asks. Please find below a concise annotated matrix and a short explanation for each mode; I attached a spreadsheet and an evidence-summary PDF to this thread (see attachments). I also uploaded a sample VPC topology image to the shared drive link.

High-level matrix (short form):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood operates the control plane and inference runtime in our managed cloud. Evidence we provide: SOC 2 report, runtime logs (redactions applied), model catalog and performance profiles, per-tenant usage logs for investigations. Customer responsibility: customer data within prompts/inputs; network controls only for API egress to Redwood endpoints.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Capacity is reserved in Redwood-managed pools that are logically isolated per customer. Evidence we provide: per-tenant telemetry, dedicated pool audit logs, deployment audit trail, and can provide configuration of isolation boundaries. Customer responsibility: application-layer access controls and customer-managed keys if opted (bring-your-own-key supported).

- Private / VPC / On-prem: Control plane remains customer-managed (or in a Red wood-managed control plane deployed into the customer VPC depending on the contract). Evidence we provide: deployment manifests, runtime logs (streamed to customer logging endpoints), and architectural diagrams. Customer responsibility: underlying network perimeter, cloud account permissions, and key management (KMS/HSM). For fully on-prem installs, Redwood provides an installer package and runbook; operational logs can be exported for SIG review.

Notes and common SIG mappings:
- Data residency and log custody: Hosted = Redwood retains logs per our retention policy (we can produce retention ranges and sample logs); Dedicated = logs are segregated and retained per contract; Private = logs are controlled by the customer except for optional agent-forwarded telemetry.
- Access controls: we map SIG access-control items to our IAM + RBAC model and to the customer's cloud IAM when Private.
- Encryption: TLS in transit and encryption at rest for hosted/dedicated (keys managed by Redwood or customer-managed if requested). Private: customer-managed keys are typical.

Attachments in this email: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx (annotated per SIG section), hosted-dedicated-private_evidence_summary.pdf, network_topology_VPC_example.png

I'll highlight a few specific SIG question examples and our suggested evidence links in the spreadsheet.

If you want, Evelyn can jump into a short call to walk through the matrix with your SIG owner.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

-----On Fri, May 4, 2028 at 13:22 Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai> wrote:-----

Connor — adding a quick technical note you can share with Marta about runtime separation and caching.

Hi Marta (cc: Connor, Karthik, Laura),

Two quick clarifications that often come up in SIGs:
1) KV/Prefix caching and Dedicated: with Dedicated pools we can configure per-tenant cache namespaces. That means any prefix/KV cache entries are logically tagged and traced to the tenant id; the evidence we provide for SIG is the cache namespace config and access logs showing namespace assignments.
2) Private/VPC: if you want log aggregation into an existing collection (e.g., your SIEM), we provide a lightweight forwarder that ships logs over mutual-TLS to your collector endpoint; the forwarder can be configured to exclude prompt/response payloads if you need minimal surface area.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the spreadsheet line-by-line.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Infra Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
